result:
I'd make other people's inner lives feel as real to everyone as their own does.

I don't mean agreement or niceness. I mean the gut-level knowledge that the person across from you, or across the world, is as fully *there* as you are, with the same depth of fear and hope and Tuesday-afternoon boredom. Most people believe this in the abstract, but almost no one feels it consistently, and I think a huge share of cruelty depends on that gap. It's hard to bomb, defraud, or ignore someone whose reality you can't stop feeling.

I'd pick this over something like curing disease because we're already making slow progress on disease. Medicine improves and knowledge accumulates. But this capacity doesn't seem to improve with progress at all. We're vastly richer and more knowledgeable than people were a thousand years ago, and about as good as they were at treating strangers as real. It may be the bottleneck behind a lot of other problems: we often have the resources to fix things and lack the will, and the will is missing because the people affected are abstractions.

It could backfire. Feeling everyone's reality at full intensity might be paralyzing, and people might need some numbness to function. So maybe I'd turn the dial up a lot rather than all the way.

What about you? I'm curious whether you asked because you have an answer of your own.
